body.heading: A library with limited hours
paragraphs: Grandparents carry stories nobody else has: the journey to a new country, the first job, the mistake that taught them everything. Most will never offer these unprompted. They are waiting to be asked, and many quietly assume nobody is interested.
Asking is a gift in both directions. The listener gets a family history that exists nowhere else; the teller gets proof that their life is worth hearing about.

body.heading: Questions that open doors
paragraphs: Skip 'tell me about the old days' — it is too big to answer. Ask small: What did your childhood kitchen smell like? What was your first job like? What did you and your friends do for fun at my age?
Record the answers if they are willing, even just voice notes on a phone. Future relatives you will never meet will be grateful someone bothered.

description: Every grandparent is a library that will not stay open forever — and most of the collection has never been asked for.
